Note::replace¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

Note::replace(std::string_view from, std::string_view to) const -> Note

What It Does¶

Replaces every occurrence of one literal substring with another, cell by cell.

This is the direct batch-text rewrite primitive for simple substitutions:

  • renaming markers

  • fixing labels

  • replacing tokens before export

  • standardizing text fragments without invoking regex machinery

replace() is global within each cell: every literal match is rewritten. It is not a “first match only” primitive and it is not regex-aware.

Parameters¶

from

The literal substring to replace.

to

The literal replacement text.

Every cell is processed independently, and cells that do not contain the substring are left unchanged.

Neither from nor to is interpreted as regex syntax here. The method is strictly literal on both sides of the substitution.

Returns¶

Note A new Note with the same shape as the input and the requested substring substitutions applied.

Examples¶

Example 1. Rewrite a common label prefix.

auto note = pluss::make_note({"score: 75", "score: 88", "pending"});
auto out = note.replace("score", "mark");
std::cout << "replace:\n" << out << "\n";

Output¶

replace:
  [0] mark: 75
  [1] mark: 88
  [2] pending

Example 2. Replace structural separators when you want a more readable surface.

auto names = pluss::make_note({"Ada_Lovelace", "Grace_Hopper", "Linus"});
auto out = names.replace("_", " ");
std::cout << "replace_underscore:\n" << pluss::note::print(out) << "\n";

Output¶

replace_underscore:
  [0] Ada Lovelace
  [1] Grace Hopper
  [2] Linus

Example 3. Replace one marker, then inspect whether the old marker is still present.

auto note = pluss::make_note({"midterm_1", "midterm_2", "final_exam"});
auto renamed = note.replace("midterm", "exam");
auto still_old = renamed.contains("midterm");
pluss::tils::OutputEngine out;
out.writeln("replace_then_contains:");
out.writeln(renamed);
std::cout << "replace_then_contains_mask:";
for (std::uint8_t v : still_old) {
  std::cout << " " << static_cast<int>(v);
}
std::cout << "\n";

Output¶

Renamed note:

replace_then_contains:
  [0] exam_1
  [1] exam_2
  [2] final_exam

Mask after replacement:

replace_then_contains_mask: 0 0 0

Notes¶

  • replace() is literal replacement, not regex replacement.

  • The two string parameters are symmetric in the sense that both are treated as literal text. There is no overload here that interprets either side as a regex program.

  • If you only want the first or last occurrence changed, the broader Note surface also exposes specialized replacement variants such as replace_first(...) and replace_last(...).

  • This is often paired with strip when the surrounding text also needs boundary cleanup.

See Also¶

  • Note::contains: check for the substring before or after replacement.

  • Note::tex_escape: escape special characters rather than replacing a literal substring yourself.
